title: Built a market research app and looking for people to try it out
author: Own_Maybe4510
selftext:
Hey everyone, I’ve been working on a little project called Olbera and thought I’d see if anyone here would be keen to give it a try.  
It’s a market research tool that looks at stocks, ETFs, forex and crypto, and gives you a daily pick based on its analysis.  
It’s still a work in progress, and I’m trying to get some real people using it and see what they think. What’s useful, what’s shit, what could be better, all feedback is welcome.  
If anyone’s interested, you can check it out here: [https://olbera.app](https://olbera.app/)  
Would genuinely appreciate anyone willing to have a look and let me know what they think.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: a daily pick across stocks, forex and crypto is a lot of ground for one model. I'd publish every pick with a timestamp and keep the misses visible, that log is what would make me trust it.

replies.author: Own_Maybe4510
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback, so some sort of a track record/ history would be an essential feature for yourself?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: yes, for me it comes before anything else. a pick list with no dated history is a newsletter; one that keeps every miss is something I'd pay attention to. same reason I run a rule on paper first: Quantradin, a site I built, logs every paper trade a rule makes with its date. quantradin.com
